# Set B — original timed practice,20marks
Suggested time: 50 minutes — 5 reading, 40 working and 5 checking. There are 8 short-answer and 12 extended-answer indicative marks. Different emphasis from Set A; not equivalent difficulty or a validated score-comparison instrument. Paper first; reference answers later. Formative inside Week 16 lesson 1.
B1 (4): Given RoomSession.remaining initially 1 and reserve implemented as `if self.remaining < 0: raise ValueError("Full")` then `self.remaining -= 1`; OnlineSession inherits and overrides location->"Online", RoomSession.location->"Room". State output of a location-call loop on one of each (1), explain polymorphic dispatch (1), repair the reservation condition (1), specify test exposing the original fault and expected corrected behaviour (1).
B2 (4): A report INNER JOINs Resource to Loan and uses COUNT(*). Requirement is ALL resources, total loans and active loans (actual Loan row with NULL ReturnDate). Identify missing-zero-row fault (1), repair join/link (1), explain active count avoiding outer placeholder (1), predict total/active pairs (1). SQL expression allowed: COUNT(CASE WHEN l.ReturnDate IS NULL THEN l.LoanID END).
B3 (6): Write summarise(rows)->dictionary accumulating exact topic counts. Criteria: initialise/iterate/unpack (1), enforce topic non-empty string (1), enforce non-negative exact integer excluding bool (1), repeated/first-key accumulation (1), return correct mapping including empty list (1), meaningful repeated/zero/invalid tests with expected outcomes (1). Do not mutate input. Contract assumes each row is a pair; no live input interface required.
B4 (6): A flat loan sheet contains LoanID,ResourceID,ResourceLabel,CategoryID,CategoryName,MemberID,MemberName,StartDate,ReturnDate. Dependencies: LoanID->ResourceID,MemberID,dates;ResourceID->Label,CategoryID;CategoryID->Name;MemberID->Name. Explain two transitive dependencies (2), decompose into Category/Resource/Member/Loan with PK/FKs (1), justify LoanID rather than ResourceID+MemberID for repeated events and relationships (1), explain explicit rollback after a second-step domain error (1), and justify retention/recovery decisions with needed evidence rather than automatic deletion (1). Inspection is separately supplied; doesn't arise from this flat sheet.
Use command and source facts precisely. Record uncertainty, then mark/explain/retry with changed data.
